a-mostly-refused-run-reports-a-clean-cou.claim: A run where almost every image was unchecked still reports broken_image_count 0, with the unchecked count printed beside it.
a-mostly-refused-run-reports-a-clean-cou.why: Withholding the count above some share of unchecked images needs that share, and this corpus gives it no basis. There is no number to re-measure until somebody decides one.

a-truncated-crawl-decides-the-whole-site.claim: Twelve site-wide items assert eq 0 over a crawl that reports itself truncated.
a-truncated-crawl-decides-the-whole-site.why: The question is whether a site-wide assertion should be withheld on truncated input, which is a decision about twelve items rather than a measurement.

answer-block-score-and-the-parser.why: A closed narrative about a parser-dependent verdict, held by the test that asserts the two parsers agree.

article-seo-private-answers.claim: article_seo.py takes the shared author and publication-date answers; no HTML fixture disagrees with them, and neither class-matched shape produces a name or a date.

cache-cleanup-test-claimed-the-machine.why: A closed narrative about a test repair, held by the test itself.

ci-002-scope-and-title.claim: CI-002 is retitled to what one inspected URL can answer; inspecting a set of important URLs is still not built.

measured.title: Confirm Google Has Indexed the Audited URL

ci-019-and-cn-053.claim: Both items closed, CI-019 in 0.21.0 and CN-053 in 0.22.0.
ci-019-and-cn-053.why: A closed narrative. What it says stays open is a lesson about how the sweeps find things, not a defect a probe can reproduce.

class-named-comments-are-invisible.claim: A byline inside a container named only by class is read as the page's author.

cn-068-floor-and-the-good-fixture.claim: On the repaired good fixture the entry page scores 75 and both other sampled pages score 35, against a floor of 60.

credit-boundary-ignores-itemref.claim: A byline referenced into a comment by itemref is still read as the page's, and a byline the page claims by itemref from inside a comment is still dropped.

default-locale-route-tree.why: A closed narrative about a release, held by the hreflang tests it added.

duplicate-twin-items.why: A closed narrative about the report's own weighting, held by the report tests.

eeat-vocabulary-by-declared-language.claim: Three reviewed vocabularies ship — English, Lithuanian and Russian — and a page declaring any other language is read with the English one, marker for marker.

foreign-credit-keys-width.claim: The boundary is ten keys wide, and the author of a book the page is only about is still read as the page's own.

four-rulings-closed.claim: All four rulings closed in 0.25.0 and 0.26.0.
four-rulings-closed.why: A closed narrative about four registry repairs, held by their assertions.

freshness-and-foreign-dates.claim: A date inside a container named only by class or by microformats is still read as the page's own, while the declared itemprop spelling is filtered.

go-138-nondeterminism-as-first-written.claim: Superseded by the entry above it, which diagnosed the cause.
go-138-nondeterminism-as-first-written.why: Kept deliberately as the entry the diagnosis replaced. Probing it would probe the entry above.

go-138-was-never-a-flake.claim: GO-138's rule matches a named field rather than the whole serialised issue, which is what made an ephemeral port read as a 404.

gsc-scenarios-accepted-a-dead-rule.why: A closed narrative about a test repair, held by the scenarios it rewrote.

gsc-thresholds-uncalibrated.claim: Nine Search Console numbers keep their inherited values and are deliberately not relabelled measured.

image-inventory-count-on-a-page-with-no-.why: A closed narrative about a release. Its repair is held by the tests that release added, not by this file.

items-that-could-not-fail.claim: Closed in 0.50.0; the severity_vocabulary mechanism that closed it proves no item today, against the seven it named when it shipped.

kw-071-evidence-and-title.claim: KW-071 asserts summary.contested_queries eq 0 with a warn band at lte 3, and no item in the registry names the removed worst_spread this entry was written about.

measured.title: Is there evidence of keyword duplication or overuse?

line-wrapped-minified-css.claim: The pinned corpus has a minified file at 37.13 bytes per line and an authored one at 47.09, so no bytes-per-line boundary separates them.

macos-kills-a-forked-child.claim: Closed in 0.15.0 as three AST-checked rules over every subprocess call.
macos-kills-a-forked-child.why: A closed narrative. The three rules it ends with are a test in this suite, which is the reader that keeps it true.

pacing-test-never-forked.why: A closed narrative about a test repair, held by the test itself.

page-guard-is-fingerprint-based.claim: An interstitial from a vendor the guard does not recognise is scored with a warning rather than refused, because it cannot be told from a client-rendered shell.
page-guard-is-fingerprint-based.why: The claim is about pages nobody has a fingerprint for. A probe would have to invent one, and inventing the input is how a check comes to test its own assumption.

privacy-and-trust-links-boundary.claim: A commenter's privacy link and contact route no longer count as the page's own: on the page this entry was measured on, both lists are empty.

rendered-artifacts-cannot-be-re-measured.claim: An operator-supplied artifact can be bounded by age and refused for naming another page, and nothing can verify what it says about itself.
rendered-artifacts-cannot-be-re-measured.why: Nothing executable is a witness: the limit is that a file's own claims cannot be re-measured, and `touch` exists. A probe here could only assert that the flag it already has still exists.

rendered-mobile-measures-owed.claim: Horizontal scroll at a phone width and clipped or overflowing text are still absent from the rendered artifact contract, whose mobile measures are two.

russian-report-english-titles-as-first-w.claim: Superseded by the entry above it.
russian-report-english-titles-as-first-w.why: Kept deliberately as the entry the repair replaced.

russian-report-is-russian-throughout.claim: Every registry item carries a Russian title and a Russian recommendation, by id and not only by count.

te-179-and-go-134.claim: Closed, TE-179 in 0.21.0 and GO-134 in 0.23.0.
te-179-and-go-134.why: A closed narrative about two registry repairs, held by their assertions.

test-files-that-ran-part-of-themselves.why: A closed narrative about a suite repair, held by the discovery rules it fixed.

threshold-declarations-unjudged.claim: Twenty-five module-level numeric constants carry no basis and sit outside the name-based scan, and one declaration marks a regular expression rather than a number.

title-polarity-has-no-gate.claim: Seventy-four of 215 items pass only when a path is absent or bounded, over nine spellings; whether a title states the side of its subject that its assertion means is read by a person, and the entry says why no check can.

titles-thinner-than-their-assertions.claim: AR-152 asserts that robots.txt has any user-agent group at all, and CN-056 asserts one date of any kind, while both titles promise more.

verify-bots-and-the-default-claim.claim: Closed in 0.15.0; the default remains a claim, and says so.
verify-bots-and-the-default-claim.why: A closed narrative whose open half is a deliberate refusal to make a network call about a third party without being asked.

wasted-bytes-before-gzip.claim: The gzip survival rate was measured across 173 source/minified pairs, and `wasted_bytes` still multiplies raw bytes by the raw-byte savings fraction and reports against an uncompressed threshold.
